changes.text: 前两条很朴素：「內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二」。利一讲路在腹地、不至于引敌，利二讲原野开阔、坟墓与房屋容易避开。一种解释是，它们针对的是安全与迁坟拆屋的顾虑，但传文未记台谏所指何害。作者认为，值得记住的正是这半句：在一个「務宏大」的人笔下，最具体的落点是沿线的坟墓与房屋能不能绕开。

The first two are plain: "Situated in the interior, there is no fear of drawing in the enemy - benefit one; the open plains are broad, and graves and houses can easily be avoided - benefit two." Benefit one says the line lies in the interior and will not draw in an enemy; benefit two says the country is open, so graves and dwellings can easily be routed around. One reading is that they address worries about security and about moved graves and demolished homes, but the biography does not record which harms the censors meant. In the author's view, worth remembering is precisely that half-sentence: under the pen of a man the verdict calls "grand in scale," the most concrete landing point is whether the graves and houses along the route can be spared.
传文对他有一句评语：「蒞官所至，必有興作。務宏大，不問費多寡」。一种解释是，这句话与前面那份编号清单出自同一种风格——敢开大摊子，也肯把摊子一条条写出来；至于花费，评语说他不问多寡，传文并未举出具体用款数字。

The biography passes a verdict on him: "Wherever he took office, he had works begun. He aimed at the grand, and did not ask how much it cost." One reading: that verdict and the numbered list share the same style - bold enough to open big undertakings, willing to write each out item by item. As for spending, the verdict says he did not ask the amount; the biography gives no figures.
一种解释是，「厚民生」排在「徵兵、轉餉」之前，是把争议最小、也最难被驳倒的目标放在最前面：台谏说的是「鐵路之害」，而避敌、避坟庐这两条恰好是对着「害」字去答的。作者推断这种写法出于策略考虑，传文没有写他的思考过程，此处是作者的解释。

One reading: putting "enriching livelihoods" before "raising troops and forwarding supplies" sets the least contested, hardest-to-topple goal at the front. The censors spoke of "the harms of railways," and the two points about avoiding the enemy and sparing graves and houses answer precisely at the word "harms." The author infers that this drafting is tactical; the biography records no thought process, so this is the author's interpretation.
当一个团队在几套方案之间争执不下时，照这份议奏的顺序，第一步不是互相挑毛病，而是把目标的优先级公开排出来——哪个目标最大、哪个次之，白纸黑字贴在最前面；然后把每个方案的利弊写成可以逐条检验的清单，像那六条编号的“利”一样，每条都能被追问“成不成立”。

When a team is deadlocked among several plans, following this memorial's order, the first step is not to pick holes in one another but to publish the ranking of goals - which goal is greatest, which next, in black and white at the front - and then write each proposal's case as a checklist testable point by point, like those six numbered benefits, each open to the challenge: "does this hold?"
